lit.\u0027\u003c/table\u003e\u003cp class=\":
"

Antoine: log₁₀P° = A − B/(T + C). Ideal mixture: approximation without azeotropes.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eAl destilar, el resid:
"

During distillation, the residue in the flask becomes depleted in the volatile component (Rayleigh equation) and the boiling temperature rises. That is why fractions are collected: the first is the richest in the volatile component. The distillation curve shows T and the instantaneous composition of the distillate versus the fraction distilled.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl \u003cb\u003ediagr:
"

The temperature–composition diagram has two curves: the bubble curve (boiling T of a liquid of composition x) and the dew curve (vapor composition y). A staircase is built: from x go up to the vapor curve, then go down horizontally to the liquid of that composition (condensate) and repeat. Each step is a theoretical plate.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn la \u003cb\u003ede:
"

In simple distillation the vapor goes directly to the condenser: this is equivalent to one theoretical plate. The distillate is enriched in the volatile component, but is not completely separated. Setup: flask with boiling chips, head with thermometer (bulb level with the side arm), condenser with water in countercurrent (enters from below) and receiving flask.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003ecolum:
"

The fractionating column (Vigreux, packed) causes successive condensations and evaporations; each one is equivalent to a theoretical plate and enriches the vapor in the more volatile component. With more plates, the distillate is purer, but the process is slower. Use the “Theoretical plates” control to see it.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003edesti:
"

Distillation separates the components of a liquid mixture by taking advantage of the fact that the more volatile one (lower boiling point) passes into vapor in greater proportion. The vapor is condensed and collected as the distillate. For an ideal mixture, Raoult's law gives the partial pressure: Pi = xi·Pi°. The mixture boils when PA + PB = external pressure; the vapor composition is yA = xA·PA°/P.

"
